title: Degree-generated opens and pulled-back homogeneous frames
statement:
Let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $d\geq1$, and $M$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every $a\in A_d$ let $s_a\in\Gamma(X,M)$ be given, and assume these sections generate each stalk: every element of $M_x$ is a finite $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear combination of the germs $(s_a)_x$. Let $g:X\to P$ be any scheme morphism satisfying $g^{-1}D_+(a)=X_{s_a}$ for every $a\in A_d$, where $X_{s_a}$ is the nonvanishing open [def-sc-section-generating-locus]. Then the opens $W_a=X_{s_a}$ cover $X$. On each $D_+(a)$, multiplication by the homogeneous section $a$ gives an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{D_+(a)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_P(d)|_{D_+(a)}$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. On every standard subopen $D_+(h)\subseteq D_+(a)$ its inverse is multiplication by the degree-$-d$ element $a^{-1}\in A_h$; for any homogeneous relation $h^N=ca$, it is the fraction $c/h^N$, and these inverses commute with localization restrictions. On $W_a$ there are isomorphisms
$$\mathcal O_{W_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}(g^*\mathcal O_P(d))|_{W_a},\quad u\longmapsto u(1\otimes a),\qquad
\mathcal O_{W_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}M|_{W_a},\quad u\longmapsto u\,s_a.$$
Here $g^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the first section is the tensor pullback of $a$, and both sections are free generators in the sense of [def-sc-local-free-generator], on every subopen of $W_a$. The index family may be infinite, and no quasi-compactness or finite subcover is required.

source.place: Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), proof: extension to the localized graded algebra; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local bases and gluing.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and trivialize $M$ near $x$, with basis germ $e$. By stalk generation, $e=\sum_{i=1}^r u_i(s_{a_i})_x$. Write $(s_{a_i})_x=b_i e$; then $1=\sum_i u_i b_i$ in the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Its maximal ideal cannot contain every $b_i$, so some $b_i$ is a unit. Represent its inverse by a local section and shrink until its product with the coefficient of $s_{a_i}$ is $1$. Multiplication by $s_{a_i}$ is then an isomorphism on this neighbourhood. Thus $x\in X_{s_{a_i}}$ by [def-sc-section-generating-locus]. This proves that the $W_a$ cover. This argument selects only finitely many germs at each individual point, not a finite subfamily covering $X$.

source.place: Tag 01CY (lemma-s-open), local basis argument; finite stalk-generation hypothesis of the item

proof.text: Fix $a\in A_d$ and a standard open $D_+(h)\subseteq D_+(a)$. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion], $a$ is a unit in $A_h$ and $h^N=ca$ for some $N\geq1$ and homogeneous $c$. Hence $a^{-1}=c/h^N$, of degree $-d$. By [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], the structure and twist sections on this open are $(A_h)_0$ and $(A_h)_d$. The mutually inverse linear maps are $u\mapsto au$ and $v\mapsto a^{-1}v$: they map $(A_h)_0$ to $(A_h)_d$ and $(A_h)_d$ to $(A_h)_0$, since $a$ has degree $d$ and $a^{-1}$ degree $-d$, and both composites are the identity because $aa^{-1}=1$. This includes $h=a$, when the inverse is $1/a$.

source.place: Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open) (1)(a)--(d); Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), the trivializing section f

proof.text: The restrictions in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] are localization homomorphisms. They send $a$ to $a$ and $a^{-1}$ to $a^{-1}$, since the image of an inverse is the inverse of the image. Thus the maps of Step 2 commute with restrictions. Standard opens inside $D_+(a)$ form a basis, and their intersections are standard opens by clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion]. For a twist section $v$ on any open $V\subseteq D_+(a)$, form $a^{-1}v$ on each such basis open inside $V$. These sections agree on intersections by the restriction calculation, so the sheaf axiom glues them uniquely to a structure section on $V$. The identities $a(a^{-1}v)=v$ and $a^{-1}(au)=u$ hold on that basis and hence on $V$. This constructs the asserted sheaf isomorphism and proves that $a$ is a free generator in the sense of [def-sc-local-free-generator]. Different relations $h^N=ca$ give the same inverse, since each represents the unique inverse of $a$ in $A_h$.

source.place: Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), localization formulas; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local trivialization

proof.text:
Restrict $g$ to $g_a:W_a\to D_+(a)$, possible because $g^{-1}D_+(a)=W_a$. Let $\tau:\mathcal O_{D_+(a)}\to\mathcal O_P(d)|_{D_+(a)}$ be Step 3 and let $\lambda=\tau^{-1}$. The tensor definition [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] on this inverse-image open gives inverse maps
$$u\longmapsto u\otimes a,\qquad u\otimes t\longmapsto u\,g_a^\sharp(\lambda(t)).$$
The second formula is balanced over $g_a^{-1}\mathcal O_{D_+(a)}$ by linearity of $\lambda$. It therefore defines a map of tensor presheaves and then their sheafifications. The first composite is $u\mapsto u\,g_a^\sharp(1)=u$; the other sends $u\otimes t$ to $u\,g_a^\sharp(\lambda(t))\otimes a=u\otimes\lambda(t)a=u\otimes t$. These identities descend to sheafification. Inverse image and tensor sheafification restricted to $W_a$ use precisely the same local sections as $g_a$, so this tensor sheaf is $(g^*\mathcal O_P(d))|_{W_a}$. The image of $1$ is $1\otimes a$. The formulas commute with restriction, giving bijections on every subopen and thus the required free generator [def-sc-local-free-generator].

source.place: Tag 0095 (definition-pushforward), pullback formula (2); explicit tensor inverse for the frame in Tag 01N8 (constructions, lemma-converse-construction)

proof.text: By [def-sc-section-generating-locus], $W_a=X_{s_a}$ is the union of the opens $U_i$ on which $s_a|_{U_i}$ is a free generator. It is a free generator on the whole union: for an open $V\subseteq W_a$, if $rs_a|_V=0$ then each $r|_{V\cap U_i}=0$, so $r=0$ by the sheaf axiom for $\mathcal O_X$; for $m\in\Gamma(V,M)$ the unique $r_i$ with $r_is_a=m$ on $V\cap U_i$ agree on overlaps by this injectivity and glue to $r$ with $rs_a|_V=m$. Hence $u\mapsto u s_a$ gives $\mathcal O_{W_a}\simeq M|_{W_a}$, with bijective section maps on every subopen, as required by [def-sc-local-free-generator]. Together with Steps 1--4 this proves every clause. Empty $W_a$ require only the unique maps of sheaves on the empty open. No step has selected a finite subcover or assumed quasi-compactness.
